Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Safeguard matrix + acceptance proofwork for evaluation run

Hi Lily / Tom —

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our conversation, attached is a concise set of artifacts to make the evaluation deterministic and reviewable by your stakeholders:

- A working MAP (mutual action plan) draft with owners and dates.
- A Safeguard Matrix (xlsx) that lists acceptance gates, measurement method, and pass/fail thresholds.
- An Acceptance Proofwork checklist (pdf) that your engineering and procurement teams can sign off.

Key asks from your side: can you confirm the two scenario priorities below so we lock test vignettes?
1) Live chat routing (latency SLO: P95 < 250ms, concordance > 92% across the 5k-message set)
2) Embedding-based search for triage (mean recall@10 >= 0.78 on the annotated set)

Proposed timeline (short):
- Week 1 (Aug 31–Sep 6): MAP kickoff, environment access, and baseline smoke tests.
- Week 2 (Sep 7–Sep 13): Run acceptance tests and collect proofwork artifacts.
- Week 3 (Sep 14–Sep 18): Review results; quick follow-up fixes; sign-off if thresholds met.

We included suggested fallback modes and rollback triggers in the Safeguard Matrix. If you want a more conservative pass threshold for chat latency we can bump it and extend the sampling window.

Attachments: 20260830-cardinal-safeguard-matrix.xlsx (sheet: gates), 20260830-acceptance-proofwork-checklist.pdf, 20260830-map-v1.docx

Thanks — happy to jump back on a quick 20m call to walk through the sheets.

—Rachel
Rachel Kim | Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Safeguard matrix + acceptance proofwork for evaluation run

Rachel —

Appreciate the clear artifacts. A couple quick clarifications before we confirm the kickoff:

1) For the chat latency SLO: the 250ms P95 is acceptable but we need a second measurement on tail latency (P99). Can you add P99 and a recommended mitigation (quantization + batching config) if P99 spikes?

2) For embeddings: the annotated set you referenced — is that the one we uploaded last quarter (dataset_v3_annotated.csv)? If so, Tom will validate consistency; if not, please point to the set you used.

Procurement note: procurement@cardinalhealth.com — we need the evaluation paperwork and a short statement on data handling (retention, logs, and SOC2 evidence). Can you attach a brief one-page summary we can include with our internal review?

Lily
Lily Park | Product Lead, CareOps | Cardinal Health
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Lily Park <lily.park@cardinalhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@cardinalhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Safeguard matrix + acceptance proofwork for evaluation run

Thanks Lily — great points. Short answers:

- P99: added. We included a P99 line in the Safeguard Matrix and listed mitigations (enable smaller batch sizes for low-concurrency, KV-cache warming, and optional int8 quant to reduce tail spikes). See column "mitigation_when_tail" in the xlsx.

- Annotated set: yes, that is dataset_v3_annotated.csv — Tom, please confirm but that is the baseline we used when estimating recall targets. If you need us to run a fresh split we can do so; it'll add 2 business days for re-annotation checks.

- Data handling one-pager: attached as an abbreviated SOC2 + retention summary (we focused on logs retention, access controls, and optional field-level masking). Attachment: 20260830-data-handling-onepager.pdf

Small edit to the MAP: moved the environment access task to Day 0 (owner: Cardinal Health infra) so we don't block Week 1 smoke tests.

If procurement can confirm the one-pager meets their requirements, can we lock kickoff for Thu Sep 2 at 10:00am PT? I'll send a calendar invite once confirmed.

—Rachel

Confirmed — procurement reviewed the one-pager and it's sufficient for the evaluation window. We're good to kickoff today at 10:00am PT; Tom and I will be on the call.
